name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Require ml_dtypes 0.7.0 in JAX and drop fallbacks for older versions

head_commit.message:
Require ml_dtypes 0.7.0 in JAX and drop fallbacks for older versions

JAX guarded `int1`, `uint1`, `bcomplex32`, `complex32` and `float8_e5m3fnu` behind `hasattr` and `is not None` checks, because ml_dtypes 0.5 does not define them. ml_dtypes 0.6.0 added the 1-bit integer and 32-bit complex types, and 0.7.0 added `float8_e5m3fnu`.

Raise the minimum ml_dtypes version to 0.7.0, the current release, and define these types unconditionally. This removes the optional typing in `jax._src.dtypes`, the `try`/`except ImportError` re-exports in `jax.numpy`, and the matching guards in the lowering code, test utilities and tests. Stale `None` checks for `int2`, `float4_e2m1fn` and `float8_e8m0fnu` are removed too.

Two workarounds for old ml_dtypes releases are also removed: the `numpy<2.4.0` pin in the array API workflow, and the upcast of small integer types before comparing arrays in the test utilities.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Accept the whole sm_107f family in `FragmentedArray` arch checks.

The PTX ISA lists the packed 8-bit integer `add`/`sub`/`neg`/`min`/`max` instructions and the `.rz` rounding mode of `cvt` to `e4m3x2`/`e5m2x2`/`e2m1x2` as supported on "sm_107f or higher in the same family". The guards for these compared the architecture to exactly sm_107, so they would have rejected a later member of the family.

This does not change behavior on any currently supported GPU.

display_title: Report breakdown in bicgstab instead of silently returning NaN

head_commit.message:
Fix bicgstab silently returning NaN on breakdown

Detect non-finite rho/alpha/omega as breakdowns (in addition to exact
zeros), keep the last finite iterate instead of the NaN update, and
report the breakdown through info following SciPy's convention:
-10 for a rho breakdown, -11 for an alpha/omega breakdown, 0 otherwise.
Previously a zero denominator made alpha inf, omega and x NaN, and the
loop exited silently returning (NaN, None).

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Use the new XLA autotuner cache flags for the persistent compilation cache.

XLA deprecated `xla_gpu_per_fusion_autotune_cache_dir` and `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_cache_mode` in favor of backend-neutral `xla_autotune_cache_dir` and `xla_autotune_cache_mode`.

Expose the new autotune cache `DebugOptions` fields in jaxlib and bump `jaxlib_extension_version` to 526. When jaxlib is new enough, JAX's persistent compilation cache now sets the new fields, and the cache key ignores them (both in `DebugOptions` and in `XLA_FLAGS`) the same way it already ignores the deprecated ones, so users switching to the new flags don't get cache misses. Older jaxlib versions keep using the deprecated fields.

The on-disk subdirectory name and the `jax_persistent_cache_enable_xla_caches` option values are unchanged, so existing caches and configurations keep working.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] Reduce scipy_stats_test_cpu_x32 generated cases to 40

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Reduce scipy_stats_test_cpu_x32 generated cases to 40

`scipy_stats_test_cpu_x32` runs 6,091 parameterized test cases (121-122 per shard across 50 shards) under the default `--jax_num_generated_cases=90`. A prior change set `--jax_num_generated_cases=40` under `"cpu"` in `backend_variant_args`, which only matches `scipy_stats_test_cpu`. Because `scipy_stats_test_cpu_x32` matches the `"cpu_x32"` config key, it kept running 57% more tests per shard than `scipy_stats_test_cpu`. With assertions enabled, it regularly timed out at the 300s medium limit.

Add `"cpu_x32": ["--jax_num_generated_cases=40"]` to `backend_variant_args` for `scipy_stats_test` (matching `sparse_test`). This reduces `scipy_stats_test_cpu_x32` to 3,607 cases (72-73 per shard) and cuts shard wall time by more than half (median 59.2s, p90 79.3s, max 97.8s across 100 shards).

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [pallas][fuser] Support sliced ref accumulation (`y_ref[s] += z`) in output fusions

head_commit.message:
[pallas][fuser] Support sliced ref accumulation (`y_ref[s] += z`) in output fusions

Previously, fusing a sliced accumulation such as `y_ref[8:16] += z` failed in
`pull_block_spec` with `ValueError: Fusion contains a DAG, cannot uniquely pull
block specs`. State discharge lowers sliced `+=` into `dynamic_slice(y, ...)`
followed by `dynamic_update_slice(y, x_old + z, ...)`. Although
`_dynamic_update_slice_eval_rule` ignores operand 0 (`y`) and
`_dynamic_update_slice_usage_rule` assigns it empty usage,
`_dynamic_update_slice_rule` returned `None` (conflating "unused by this
equation" with "needed unblocked"). That collided with the `BlockIndexTransform`
pulled from `dynamic_slice`, even when `strict_mode=False`.

Changes:
- Separate unused operands from unblocked operands during pull propagation via
  an `_unused` sentinel returned by `_dynamic_update_slice_rule` for operand 0
  (and by `_call_jaxpr_pull_block_spec_rule` for unused nested invars), skipped
  in `_pull_block_transform` so write-only slices still default to
  `no_block_spec` while read-modify-write slices retain the pulled transform.
- Use explicit subtraction (`negate=True`) in `_offset_indexer` for
  `_dynamic_update_slice_rule` instead of negating `clamped_starts` before
  floor division.
- Validate aliased input/output `BlockSpec` agreement in `pull_block_spec` /
  `push_pull_block_spec` (propagating `output_input_aliases` from
  `get_stateful_output_fusion_values`) by comparing pulled `BlockIndexTransform`s
  using a pure CSE + constant-folding + add/sub cancellation index-map
  normalizer (and rejecting partial `dynamic_update_slice` updates on aliased
  outputs whose base operand is not the aliased input `Ref` directly), so
  matching sliced accumulations pass under `strict_mode=True` while mismatched,
  overlapping, or multi-write read/write slices (e.g.,
  `y_ref[128:256] = y_ref[0:128] + z`) are rejected.
- Add unit tests in `fuser_block_spec_test.py` and end-to-end TPU stateful
  matmul tests in `tpu_fusible_matmul_with_stateful_fusions_test.py`.

head_commit.message:
Fix batched column permutation in pivoted QR JVP.

In `qr_jvp_rule`, `x[..., p[0]]` and `dx[..., p[0]]` assumed `p[0]` was 1D. For inputs with leading batch dimensions, `p[0]` has shape `(*batch_dims, n)`, causing advanced indexing to broadcast the batch dimensions rather than permuting columns per batch element.

Use `api.vmap` over leading batch dimensions when permuting `x` and `dx` by `p[0]`, and add a `LaxLinalgTest.test_batched_pivoted_qr_jvp` test covering batched wide, square, and tall matrices.

head_commit.message:
Donate PjRt-IFRT executable inputs according to donation intent.

`LoadedExecutable::GetDonatableInputIndices()` reports parameter donation intent (`jax.buffer_donor` and `tf.aliasing_output`), whereas XLA compilation may leave a donor unaliased when no compatible output buffer exists. Because post-compilation buffer aliasing is unpredictable to callers, `PjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute()` marks all inputs in `donatable_input_indices` (unless in `ExecuteOptions::non_donatable_input_indices`) as deleted after dispatch.

Bump `JAX_XLA_VERSION_NUMBER` to 90 and update JAX buffer donation tests to expect donated inputs to be deleted without aliasing.

older jaxlib), and computing multi-process metadata lazily. Existing
ndarray callers are unaffected.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [JAX] Support equality comparison between JAX `DeviceList` and Python `tuple`

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Support equality comparison between JAX `DeviceList` and Python `tuple`

Comparing a JAX `DeviceList` against a Python `tuple` of devices immediately returned `False` because `PyDeviceList::Equal` rejected any object that was not itself a `PyDeviceList`. Rich-comparison dispatch also had two defects: `__eq__` and `__ne__` lacked `nb::is_operator()` (raising `TypeError` on `None`) and returned `bool` instead of `NotImplemented` for unsupported types (preventing Python from invoking reflected RHS `__eq__`/`__ne__` such as `unittest.mock.ANY`).

Update `PyDeviceList::Equal` and `PyDeviceList::NotEqual` to return `nb::not_implemented()` for unsupported types (preserving existing `.pyi` signatures via `nb::sig`), and accept exact Python `tuple` objects (`PyTuple_CheckExact`) for element-by-element comparison after an O(1) length check, stopping at the first mismatch. Rejecting `tuple` subclasses keeps equality symmetric and consistent across `index() == 0` and `index() == 1` without extra subclass-handling machinery.

For IFRT-backed device lists, exact ready `PyDevice` elements are compared via `PyClient*` and `xla::ifrt::Device*` pointers without allocating `PyDevice` wrappers, copying tuples, or constructing temporary IFRT `DeviceList` objects—avoiding both Python object materialization overhead and backend `MakeDeviceList` exceptions on duplicate or cross-device-set tuples (e.g., under Pathways). Non-`PyDevice` or uninitialized elements fall back to Python rich comparison. The `Hash()` fast-path in `DeviceList`-vs-`DeviceList` comparison is scoped to `case 0` only so comparing two tuple-backed `DeviceList` instances with unhashable duck-typed elements does not raise `TypeError` or pay unnecessary tuple hashing.

Empty IFRT-backed `DeviceList` instances are aligned in both `Hash()` (hashing to `hash(())`) and `Equal()` (short-circuiting empty checks before delegating to backend `ifrt::DeviceList::operator==`, so empty IFRT-backed lists compare equal consistently across different backends such as `BasicDeviceList` and Pathways `DeviceList`). Non-empty IFRT-backed `DeviceList` instances continue to hash via `absl::HashOf` rather than Python's `tuple` hash to avoid materializing `PyDevice` wrappers on hash, so mixing `DeviceList` with `tuple` keys—or mixing cross-representation `DeviceList` keys (`index() == 0` vs `index() == 1`)—in the same `dict` or `set` remains unsupported.

`xla_client._version` is bumped to `526` to gate the new `device_test.py` tests against older `jaxlib` wheels during compatibility testing.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [ROCm] Edit testScaledMatmul against an fp32 accumulation bound on GPUs gfx11

head_commit.message:
Check testScaledMatmul against an fp32 accumulation bound on gfx11

The bfloat16 variants of testScaledMatmul fail on RDNA3 (gfx1100/1101/1103)
by one bfloat16 ulp. The reference is rounded to the output dtype, and RDNA3
v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_{bf16,f16} does not accumulate bit-exactly in fp32, so
results whose exact value is a bfloat16 tie may round to the other neighbour.
Both the Triton and hipBLASLt GEMMs use this instruction.

On gfx11, instead of tuning rtol/atol, require every output to lie between the
dtype roundings of exact +- K * 2^-24 * sum|a*b|, the standard bound for any
fp32 accumulation order. Away from a rounding boundary this demands the exact
RNE result, so the check is stricter than rtol=1e-3 for most elements. Other
platforms keep the existing tolerance check; the bound check is valid for any
fp32 accumulation, so it can be enabled everywhere by dropping the gfx11
condition.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Add a mechanism to set IFRT custom options for JAX functions

head_commit.message:
Add jax.execution_options for per-call IFRT execute options

Expose ifrt::ExecuteOptions::custom_options from JAX via a
jax.execution_options(custom_options=...) context manager. Options set
inside the context are forwarded to every execution dispatched from the
current thread, for both jitted and AOT-compiled functions, through the
C++ fast path and the Python fallback.

The options are stored in a regular jax config (thread-local with a
global fallback) as a plain dict and converted to an AttributeMap in C++
on dispatch. They are not part of the jit cache key, so changing them
never retraces or recompiles. Nested contexts merge, inner values win.
Supported value types are bool, int, float, str and sequences of int.

Bump jaxlib_extension_version to 526.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support K=96 block-scaled FP4 tcgen05.mma with 128-lane A scales.

Dense 4-bit block-scaled `tcgen05.mma` only used `K=96` steps when A scales were in `scales_layout()`. On `sm_107f`, layout inference prefers `scales_128_lane_layout()` for A scales, so those MMAs fell back to `K=64` steps and issued up to 1.5× more MMA instructions per K tile than needed.

`tcgen05.mma` now also uses `K=96` steps when A scales are in `scales_128_lane_layout()`. The requirements on B scales are unchanged.
